chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Washsha from Aban from Maymun al-Qaddah said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Read.' I said, 'From which thing should I read?' He said, 'From the ninth Chapter.' So I began to seek it, so he said, 'Read from Surah Yunus.'
For those who do good is the best [reward] and extra, and no darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I am astonished at how I do not grow gray when I recite the Quran.''

key_terms.السُّورَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ: The ninth chapter (Surah Al-Imran), often cited in early contexts before the final numbering was standardized or referring to a specific recitation context.
key_terms.سُورَةِ يُونُسَ: Surah Yunus (Chapter 10), from which the quoted verse is taken.
key_terms.لَأَعْجَبُ: I am astonished/wondering, expressing amazement at a spiritual phenomenon.
key_terms.لَا أَشِيبُ: I do not grow gray, referring to the preservation of youth or vitality.
key_terms.لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا: For those who do good, a phrase indicating the reward for righteous deeds.
key_terms.وَزِيَادَةٌ: And extra [reward], indicating additional blessings beyond the primary reward.
key_terms.وَلَا يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ: And no darkness will cover their faces, indicating purity and light.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet's reaction to reciting the Quran regarding aging and spiritual vitality?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir guides Maymun al-Qaddah to recite the opening verses of Surah Yunus (10:26), which promise 'the best' (al-husna) and freedom from humiliation for the righteous. The narration concludes with the Prophet Muhammad’s reflection on the spiritual vitality that prevents him from aging during Quranic recitation, a concept often interpreted in Shia tradition as a sign of the enduring freshness of divine revelation and the Imam's unique connection to it.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Aban, from Maymoun Al Qaddah who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Read!’. I said, ‘From which thing?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the ninth Chapter’. So I went on to seek it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Read from Surah Yunus (Chapter 10).
So I recited [10:26] For those who do good is good and more; neither darkness nor disgrace shall cover their faces.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> am astonished how I<sup>saww</sup> do not age when I<sup>saww</sup> recite the Quran’.
en.sarwar: 19. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from Aban from Maymun al-Qaddah who has said the following:

“Once abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to me, ‘Read.’ I then asked, ‘What should I read?’ The Imam said, ‘Read from Chapter 9.’ I (the narrator) tried to find it but he said, ‘Read from Yunus (which is Chapter 10).’
I (the narrator) then read: ‘The righteous will receive good rewards for their deeds and more. Their faces will suffer no disgrace or ignominy. . . .’ [10:26]
The Imam said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “It is astonishing to me, why should I not grow old much quicker when I read the Holy Quran.’”
